note: Changes to the model or the data process, each tied to the graded result or data problem that prompted it. Newest first.

lessons.saw: Three of the six Copa del Rey ties on 18 Nov went to extra time. Mallorca won 3-1 at Alcoyano after extra time, but the builder 'Mallorca to win + Over 1.5 goals' lost on the 1-1 at 90 minutes. Minera v Cartagena (2-1 to Cartagena after extra time) had no published 90-minute score by the next morning, and none of the six EuroCup and Champions League games from 18 Nov had a final score that could be opened.
lessons.change: Cup ties are graded on the 90-minute score only, and a leg whose 90-minute outcome isn't published waits in gradingTodo instead of being guessed. Basketball and hockey day files can carry gradingTodo too (the 18 Nov European basketball games).

lessons.saw: 18 Nov best bets: NBA/NHL 2 of 5 (Heat under, Warriors +6, Avalanche lost), Copa del Rey 'fair price' best bets at -0.2% and -1.7%. Re-scoring all 127 priced legs graded so far: the bookmaker's own price, margin removed, predicted results better than the model (Brier 0.245 vs 0.267), and legs where the model claimed a 3%+ edge won 46% against 66% predicted.
lessons.change: Every probability is now anchored to its price: the model keeps 30% of its disagreement (60% when late team news hasn't reached the price). The best bet needs a +1% edge after that, so it becomes a rare 'Value bet'. Each game now shows its most likely outcome with fair odds, and every pick shows the minimum odds worth taking.

lessons.saw: The user bets at Meridian. On 18 Nov its prices on the site's picks were far below Pinnacle's: Heat under 1.71 vs 1.94, Warriors +6.5 1.68 vs +6 at 1.95, Avalanche 1.88 vs 2.01. A small edge at Pinnacle is a 5-12% loss at those prices.
lessons.change: 'Min odds' replaces 'Fair' on every bet slip row and on the best bet: below it, skip the bet. Odds refreshes now retire team-news adjustments once the new price contains them, so injuries aren't counted twice.

lessons.saw: Night one of NBA: best bets went 2 of 4. Pistons +9.5 and Wolves won. Raptors +2.5 lost, and both other losers came from the two games whose spread prices weren't published, so the model used 1.91: Lakers -8.5 (the real price had moved to 2.09, and they won by 4 in OT) and Clippers to win at 65%, a row with no price that lost by 25.
lessons.change: Markets with an assumed price are marked "price assumed" and can be Lean at most. They can never be the best bet. A moneyline row with no price needs 72% instead of 64% to be more than Skip. On 19 Nov this turns two fake edges into No bet: Warriors +6.5 had shown +9.8%, and that was a guessed price.

lessons.saw: Night one of NHL: puck-line best bets went 4 of 5, all underdog +1.5. The loser, Capitals +1.5, lost by 3. The scoring model had no idea that a team trailing by one pulls its goalie, which turns many one-goal wins into two-goal wins. It also expected too few games to go to overtime (16% vs about 23% in the NHL).
lessons.change: The pre-match score grid now adds pulled-goalie goals. When a side trails by one, the leader scores again 22% of the time and the trailer ties it 10%. When it trails by two, the figures are 15% and 7%. Underdog +1.5 chances drop about a point, overtime is up to 19-20%, and overs and team totals go up a little. Tonight Canadiens +1.5 drops to No bet. Avalanche–Mammoth Over 6.5 becomes the hockey best bet.

lessons.saw: The 17 Nov props were graded the next morning, after the evening session had switched props to per-stat calibration. Re-running the new engine would have recorded chances the page never showed: Pedro Neto 1+ shots at 88% instead of 79%, Yasin Ayari 1+ shots at 84% instead of 76%, Callum Styles 1+ shots at 24% instead of 30%.
lessons.change: Legs are graded with the engine as it was on match day (the version before any later change, from git) and results.json as it stood before that day's legs, so the track record holds the chances the page actually showed. The 22 remaining 17 Nov legs were graded this way (13 won); fouls and tackles props stayed ungraded because no full per-player source had them.

lessons.saw: After 61 graded props the lumped "Player prop" line looked fine (61% predicted, 59% landed), but it hid opposite errors: shots props landed 18/27 (67%) against 60% predicted, while shots-on-target props landed 11/20 (55%) against 65% and fouls 6/13 (46%) against 57%. On 17 Nov the user's own low-line shot legs (Scales 1+ shot, Vitinha 1+ on target) landed again.
lessons.change: Props are now also tracked per stat (shots, shots on target, fouls, tackles). Once a stat has 8 graded props it gets its own calibration, so shots props are stretched and on-target and foul props trimmed; until then the shared Player prop line is used. The track record shows the per-stat rows under Player prop.

lessons.saw: On 15 Nov, ESPN's player stats and player game logs gave complete shot, shot-on-target and fouls-committed lines, which settled 24 of the 48 priced props (16 won). The 16 tackle props for players who played stayed ungraded because ESPN only lists 'defensive interventions' and Sofascore would not load. Latvia v Armenia's ESPN pages only loaded as a 32nd-minute snapshot, so its 4 props were left out even though two of them showed as landed.
lessons.change: Shot, shot-on-target and foul props are graded from ESPN's player stats and game logs, after checking that the player rows add up to the team totals. Tackle props stay ungraded until a full per-player source is found. When a match's pages only load as an in-game snapshot, all of its props are left out, wins and losses alike, so the track record isn't tilted toward props that landed early.

lessons.saw: No reachable source had full per-player fouls or tackles for the 56 priced props on 14 Nov. Partial live feeds and bookings could only prove that a prop had landed (a booking for a foul proves 1+ fouls) and never that it had lost. Grading everything they could settle would have recorded 12 wins from 13 props and inflated the prop track record.
lessons.change: A prop is graded only from a source that lists every shot, shot on target, foul or tackle for that player, such as an ESPN shot map or a box-score stat line, so that a loss would show up as clearly as a win. Props that only a partial feed can settle stay ungraded. On 14 Nov that left 7 graded props (6 won).

lessons.saw: Ten research agents shared one search budget of about 200 searches and ran out partway through, so several props have no per-90 rates and some XIs have only one source. Typed KickOff URLs were also refused; only links that came back from a search could be opened.
lessons.change: Each match agent searches for its KickOff and statz.ai pages first, opens the links the search returns, and keeps to about 15 searches so every match gets covered.

lessons.saw: Japan v Brazil kicked off at 11:15 Warsaw. By then the morning run had found no bookmaker prices and no team sheets for it.
lessons.change: Games that kick off before noon Warsaw are researched first, in their own quick pass. If they still have no prices, they are left off the page.

lessons.saw: The data check priced picks without the track-record adjustment the site applies, so it could report a different best bet from the page.
lessons.change: The check now loads results.json first, so it prints the same best bets the page shows.

lessons.saw: KickOff lists bet365 prices as fractions (11/20, 10/3), and two research passes could not open the page at all.
lessons.change: Fractions are converted to decimals (11/20 becomes 1.55). If KickOff can’t be read, the run tries it again before using another site, and the odds note names the bookmaker and the site.

lessons.saw: Argentina v Uruguay kicks off at 23:00 UK time, which is midnight in Warsaw.
lessons.change: Matches are filed by their Warsaw date, so a midnight kick-off goes on the next day’s page.

lessons.saw: One source listed Florian Wirtz at 2.15 fouls per 90, which looked like fouls won rather than fouls committed.
lessons.change: Foul props only use fouls committed. A figure above about 1.5 per 90 for an attacking player is checked against a second source before it is used.

lessons.saw: Some sources count a player’s shots over more games than the team totals beside them, which inflates his share of the team’s chances.
lessons.change: Team totals must cover the same games as the player counts, or they are left out.

lessons.saw: 4 of 5 props lost, including 1+ shot on target for Anthony Gordon (1.30) and Fermín López (1.29). Those prices need the bet to land 77% of the time.
lessons.change: Each prop now gets its own chance from the player’s per-90 rates, or a cautious position average, and is only marked Bet when that chance beats the price.

lessons.saw: France to win + Over 1.5 goals lost when Italy won 3-1. France were only a 46% favourite. Builders on 55%+ favourites won 2 of 3.
lessons.change: A builder only includes a result leg when the favourite is 55% or more. Otherwise it is built from double chance, goals and BTTS legs.

lessons.saw: Two -1.5 handicaps had no bookmaker price. Spain’s won 2-0; England’s lost on a 2-1 win.
lessons.change: Handicaps without a bookmaker price stop at -1, which refunds the stake on a one-goal win.

lessons.saw: Over 7.5 corners in Italy v France and England to win the corner count both lost. Neither had a bookmaker line to anchor it.
lessons.change: Corner and card chances priced without a bookmaker line are pulled 20% closer to 50/50.

lessons.saw: The best-bet tile could show a pick whose price was shorter than the model’s fair odds, so backing it had no edge.
lessons.change: The best bet must be priced between 1.35 and 3.50 and within 2% of fair value or better. When nothing qualifies, the card says No bet.

lessons.saw: Picks were shown but never graded, so nothing told the model which markets it overrated.
lessons.change: Every graded pick goes into the track record. Once a market has 8 results, its chances are pulled toward 50/50 if it lands less often than promised, or stretched if it lands more often.
